items.title: Bob Watts Interview, 1963-02-28
items.q: And then they wanted me to feature myself now and then... and we'd get that man, and one of the players could double on the mandolin. And we'd get back there, that ball man, I swear, and when we'd start jamming them numbers... Addison McQueen didn't have no banjo, he had a guitar man, see? And we'd

ctx.x: Yeah, see. In the 30's, you see.

Yeah, but nothing but money, plenty of money. Plenty of money, plenty of money in circulation. We made a lot of tips, 1750 was the salary, but you made a lot of tips. Oh, that was good, Sam. You made a lot of tips, see. Yeah, tips, yeah. Well alright, I got Harrison Wood there with Tommy Brooks and his brother, I didn't like the idea of Gene Brooks, that's the banjo man, that was Tommy's brother. See, Tommy on piano and the poor on banjo, and I don't know, they looked like they wanted to have their way about…
Yeah. You talk about him all the time.
